title: RouteDecision explainability record (v1)
description: The explainability record every route produces (design.md §12). It is derived from router inputs, router scores, and router policy. It is not derived from hidden model reasoning, and the router must not expose or attempt to generate such reasoning. WHAT THIS SCHEMA BOUNDS, precisely: every string property is length-capped and character-class-constrained, and every numeric property has a finite range, so the record has a bounded maximum serialized size and no field accepts arbitrary bytes. `root_session_hash` accepts only a 64-character lowercase hex digest (a local-salt digest, ADR-0004, design.md §13.1); `decision_id` is anchored at both ends; `lane_id`, candidate ids, and `selected` are bounded identifier tokens; `model_card_version` and `router_version` are 64-character version tokens; `excluded[].reasons[]` is the widest channel at 200 characters per entry, at most 8 entries per exclusion and at most 64 exclusions. WHAT THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT BOUND: value constraints bound the SHAPE of what can be written, not the INTENT of what is written. A 200-character diagnostic field will hold 200 characters of prompt text; a 128-character identifier will hold a credential that happens to be alphanumeric; a bounded field repeated across many array entries aggregates. This schema therefore cannot and does not establish that the record carries no prompt text, no tool results, and no credential values. That exclusion is a WRITE-PATH INVARIANT: it is established by the Phase 8 code that constructs these records, which populates `reasons[]` from limits, policy, and health rather than from request content, and it is that code — not this file — that must be reviewed and tested for it. Phase 1 ships no write path, so nothing here is reachable today. `selected` is not constrained to equal `ranked[0].candidate`, because a health veto (design.md §7.10) legitimately selects a lower-ranked candidate, and `ranked` may be empty when every candidate was hard-excluded, in which case `excluded` carries the explanation and `selected` is null.

decision_id.description: Opaque decision identifier, prefixed `dec_` (design.md §12). Anchored at BOTH ends and length-capped; a prefix-only `^dec_` would have accepted `dec_` followed by an arbitrary payload. The suffix class includes `_` and `-` so the obvious generators are usable: `"dec_" + str(uuid4())` and snake_case test ids both validate. Widening the class does not weaken the field — the anchoring and the 64-character cap are what bound it, not the exclusion of two punctuation characters.

root_session_hash.description: The root session identifier hashed with a local salt, not the raw Hermes session id (ADR-0004, design.md §13.1). The pattern admits only a 64-character lowercase hex digest, so this field rejects a raw session id, a prompt, and any value containing a character outside `[0-9a-f]` — the tightest constraint in this schema, and one a fixed-width digest is genuinely equivalent to. It does not distinguish a correctly salted digest from any other 64 hex characters; that the value is in fact `sha256(salt + session_id)` is a property of the code that computes it. The salt is local, so digests are not correlatable across machines.

lane_id.description: Opaque lane identifier within the root session (design.md §6.2, ADR-0002). Bounded length and an identifier-only character class keep it a handle rather than a text field.

cache_epoch.description: Cache epoch of the lane at decision time (design.md §6.4). Capped at 2^31-1: JSON integers are arbitrary-precision, so an uncapped counter is an unbounded field, and no real lane approaches two billion cache epochs.

turn_id.description: User turn ordinal within the lane (design.md §6.3). Capped at 2^31-1 for the same reason as `cache_epoch`.

mode.description: The routing mode in force for this decision (design.md §4.1).

requirements.description: The predicted capability requirement vector (design.md §7.2). Properties are the eight capability dimensions, each normalized to [0, 1]. None are required: a heuristic predictor may legitimately emit only the subset of dimensions the request exercises, exactly as the design.md §12 example does. Unknown dimension names fail validation so a typo cannot silently vanish.

excluded.description: Candidates removed by hard eligibility filters, policy, or veto (design.md §7.3, §7.10). Every entry carries at least one machine-readable reason, so no exclusion is unexplained. May be empty when nothing was excluded. `maxItems` 64 bounds the array against the candidate roster it describes — a decision cannot exclude more candidates than exist — and without it the per-entry caps below aggregate without limit.

candidate.description: The `id` of the excluded candidate's model card. `maxLength` and `pattern` are byte-identical to model-card.v1 `/properties/id`; a contract test asserts that, because a divergence makes a loadable card unwritable to a decision record.

reasons.description: Non-empty list of exclusion reasons. Each is intended to be a router-authored diagnostic derived from limits, policy, or health, such as the design.md §12 example `context window 65536 < required 84211`. This is the widest string channel in the record: at most 8 entries of at most 200 characters, so at most 1,600 characters per exclusion and, with `excluded`'s `maxItems`, at most 102,400 characters per record. Those caps bound SIZE. They do not make the field content-free — 200 characters is ample for a fragment of a prompt or an error body, and 512 such fragments reassemble. What keeps request content out is the Phase 8 code that populates these strings from limits, policy, and health objects rather than from the request; the caps are a size ceiling under that invariant, not a substitute for it.

ranked.description: Hard-eligible candidates ordered by final route loss, best first (design.md §7.8). May be empty when every candidate was hard-excluded; `excluded` then explains why and `selected` is null. `maxItems` 64 matches `excluded`: together they bound the record at the size of the candidate roster.

candidate.description: The `id` of the ranked candidate's model card. `maxLength` and `pattern` are byte-identical to model-card.v1 `/properties/id`, asserted by a contract test.

shortfall.description: Weighted capability shortfall (design.md §7.4). Bounded below at 0 but deliberately unbounded above, because it is a sum of positive per-dimension deficits across weighted dimensions and can exceed 1.

final_loss.description: Final route loss used for ordering (design.md §7.8). Unbounded in both directions: penalties and bonuses may drive it negative.

estimated_cost.description: Estimated turn cost in USD (design.md §7.5). Null when the candidate's pricing is unknown — unknown is never treated as zero.

estimated_ttft_ms.description: Estimated time to first token in milliseconds (design.md §7.6). Null when no estimate is available. Capped at 24 hours — an estimate beyond that is a bug, not a slow provider.

health.description: Live health score at decision time (design.md §11.1).

switch_penalty.description: Stickiness and hysteresis penalty applied for switching away from the incumbent (design.md §7.9).

selected.description: The `id` of the selected candidate, or null for a structured failure in which no hard-eligible candidate remained. `maxLength` and `pattern` are byte-identical to model-card.v1 `/properties/id` and apply only to the string branch; JSON Schema ignores both for null, so the null case stays representable. Deliberately NOT constrained to equal `ranked[0].candidate`: a health veto (design.md §7.10) selects a lower-ranked candidate and must remain representable.

reason_codes.description: Machine-readable reason codes for this decision, drawn from the frozen twelve-code vocabulary in design.md §12. The enum is exactly twelve values; it is a frozen contract and must not be widened without a schema version bump. `minItems: 1` makes the selection path as explainable as the exclusion path — `excluded[].reasons` already requires a reason, so a decision that emitted zero reason codes would leave the *selection* unexplained. `uniqueItems` rejects the same code repeated, which is noise rather than emphasis.

model_card_version.description: The model-card snapshot version this decision was scored against, taken from the card `evidence.source_version` (ADR-0003, design.md §9.2). Present so a decision is replayable against the exact card set that produced it. The class covers semantic versions, dates, and PEP 440 local versions (`1.2.3+local.1`); `+` is included for that last form. Bounded because this and `router_version` were the two fully unconstrained strings in the record and a version token has no reason to exceed 64 characters.

router_version.description: Version of the router that produced this decision, so a behavioral change can be attributed to a specific release. Same class and cap as `model_card_version`.
